# `silk/time/duration`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Exact elapsed time: the [`Duration`](#Duration) type, a signed span of seconds and nanoseconds.

## When to use

Use [`Duration`](#Duration) for a timeout, a measured time, or the distance between two instants. It
counts real time only, so an hour is always 3600 seconds. A span in calendar units, such as
"one month", has no fixed length and is not a `Duration`.

## Details

A `Duration` holds signed whole seconds and a nanosecond part from 0 to 999,999,999. Two equal
spans always have equal fields, so `==` and `<` compare spans. `+`, `-`, unary `-`, and `*` by
an `i64` are exact and trap when the result leaves the range. The `checked` functions return
`None` instead.

## Examples

### Add two spans and read the parts

```silk
import silk.time.duration { Duration }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let total = Duration.fromSeconds(90) + Duration.fromMilliseconds(1500)
  if total.wholeSeconds() != 91 || total.subsecondNanoseconds() != 500000000 {
    return 1
  }
  if !(&Duration.fromMinutes(1) < &total) {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Duration` with `import silk.time.duration { Duration }`.

## `Duration`

```silk
pub struct Duration
```

A signed span of exact time with nanosecond precision.

### Details

The span is `wholeSeconds` seconds plus `subsecondNanoseconds` nanoseconds. The nanosecond part
is always from 0 to 999,999,999, also for a negative span: one nanosecond before zero is `-1`
second plus 999,999,999 nanoseconds. Equal spans have equal parts. The seconds cover the whole
`i64` range, about 292 billion years in each direction.

`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare spans. `+`, `-`, unary `-`, and `*` by an `i64`
trap when the result is outside the range.

<a id="Duration.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(seconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Duration
```

Returns the span of `seconds` seconds plus `nanoseconds` nanoseconds.

#### Details

Whole seconds in `nanoseconds` move into the seconds, and `nanoseconds` can be negative. So
`Duration.make(0, 1500000000)` is 1.5 seconds and `Duration.make(1, -1)` is one nanosecond
less than a second.

#### Gotchas

A total outside the `i64` seconds range traps. [`Duration.checkedMake`](#Duration.impl.checkedMake) returns `None`
instead.

#### Details

Whole seconds in `nanoseconds` move into the seconds, and `nanoseconds` can be negative.

<a id="Duration.impl.wholeSeconds"></a>

### Method `wholeSeconds`

```silk
pub fn wholeSeconds(self: Self) -> i64
```

Returns the whole seconds of the span, rounded toward negative infinity.

#### Details

The span is this value plus [`Duration.subsecondNanoseconds`](#Duration.impl.subsecondNanoseconds). For -1.5 seconds the result is
`-2`, and the nanosecond part is 500,000,000.

<a id="Duration.impl.subsecondNanoseconds"></a>

### Method `subsecondNanoseconds`

```silk
pub fn subsecondNanoseconds(self: Self) -> u32
```

Returns the nanosecond part of the span, from 0 to 999,999,999.

#### Details

The part counts forward from [`Duration.wholeSeconds`](#Duration.impl.wholeSeconds), also for a negative span. For -1.5
seconds the whole seconds are `-2` and this part is 500,000,000.

## Implementation `Display for Duration`

```silk
impl Display for Duration
```

Writes the span as an ISO 8601 duration in hours, minutes, and seconds, such as `PT1H30M`,
`PT0.5S`, or `-PT45S`. The empty span is `PT0S`.
